# Microsoft Graph

**Parity grade: B** · SDK `hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread@v3.10.0` · last audited 2026-10-31 (`666cb1c4c`)

### Known gaps

- User GET and list return only the default property set (id, businessPhones, displayName, givenName, jobTitle, mail, mobilePhone, officeLocation, preferredLanguage, surname, userPrincipalName) unless $select is given, as recalled from the Get user reference; that list and the create-response shape are not verified against the live service. Unset properties are returned as explicit nulls.
- Soft delete: deleted applications, service principals, users and groups are removed at once; /directory/deletedItems, restore and permanentDelete are not implemented.
- Not implemented: $batch, federatedIdentityCredentials, directoryRoles/roleManagement, administrativeUnits, devices, contacts, applicationTemplates, tokenIssuancePolicies, claimsMappingPolicies, delta queries, extension attributes, users/{id}/manager, photos, licensing, @odata.bind on user manager, and the $expand option (answered with 400 Request_UnsupportedQuery).
- Graph permissions are not enforced (no Authorization_RequestDenied for missing Application.ReadWrite.All and similar); requiredResourceAccess and appRoleAssignments are stored but grant nothing, and tokens carry no roles/scp claims.
- Certificate credentials: addKey does not keep the key or verify the proof, so client_assertion/certificate token requests are not supported; password users cannot sign in (no ROPC or authorization-code flow), so /me needs a hand-built user token.
- Error messages and codes not verified against the live service (recalled, not read from the reference): malformed ids ('Invalid object identifier'), duplicate identifierUris/uniqueName/UPN/servicePrincipalNames ('Another object with the same value for property ... already exists'), unknown property ('Property ... does not exist as a declared property'), the password complexity message, appRoleAssignment validation messages, group creation rules (mail-enabled and neither-flag refusals, isAssignableToRole), unsupported-method 405 code, and the 'Unable to read JSON request payload' text.
- Built-in first-party service principals: only Microsoft Graph with a subset of its roles (Application.Read[Write].All, Directory.Read[Write].All, User.Read[Write].All, Group.Read[Write].All, Mail.Send) and scopes (User.Read, openid, profile, email, offline_access). Other well-known applications (Azure Service Management, Key Vault, ...) are absent, so looking them up by appId returns 404.
- Deleting an application removes its service principal immediately, and disabling an app role that is still assigned is not refused; appRoles removal is not blocked while in use. Entra's rules for these are not verified.
- Terraform azuread fixture (application with web redirect URIs and requiredResourceAccess, service principal, application password) applies, replans empty and destroys against the container (test/terraform/azure/azuread_test.go) using metadata_host and the dev client; other azuread resources (groups, users, app role assignments, federated credentials, directory roles) are not exercised.
- ARM role assignment validation (--azure-arm-validate-principals) does not know system-assigned identities of VMs, web apps and other ARM resources, so it stays opt-in.
